item.title: Near-Theoretical-Density Zinc Plating Enabled by an Ordered Janus Interphase for High-Energy Zinc Pouch Cells

💡 The novelty is a nanometer-thin organic–inorganic Janus bilayer (CF-LaF3) that pre-engineers the zinc interface, combining desolvation, water blocking, and uniform Zn2+ flux. It enables near-theoretical-density plating (8.60 vs 8.54 μm) at 5 mAh cm–2, dendrite-free, and 109 Wh L–1 Ah-level Zn||I2 pouch cells, offering a scalable route to practical high-energy aqueous zinc batteries.
🏷 zinc metal battery · Janus interphase · dendrite-free plating · pouch cell · LaF3

item.title: Mechanistic Control of Cathode–Electrolyte Interphase Formation in Gel Polymer Electrolyte for Lithium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:

💡 This work is novel in using tris(4-fluorophenyl)phosphine (TFPP) with a tailored formation protocol to control residual monomer degradation in in-situ gel polymer electrolytes. TFPP preferentially decomposes before monomer oxidation, forming a LiF-rich inner cathode–electrolyte interphase. This suppresses side reactions and enables a 2 Ah pouch cell with 303 Wh kg⁻¹ and 82.8% retention after 150 cycles under lean electrolyte.

item.title: Escaping the Polymerization-Kinetics Trap in Ether Electrolytes for Durable Silicon Interphases
item.description:

ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in identifying a polymerization-kinetics trap: stronger polymerization in trioxane electrolytes worsens silicon interphase durability by depleting species prematurely. Adding LiNO3 suppresses early trioxane activation while enabling nitrate-derived passivation, yielding a thinner, coherent interphase. This kinetic regulation significantly improves cycling stability, offering a new design principle for durable silicon anodes.
🏷 silicon anode · ether electrolyte · solid electrolyte interphase · LiNO3 · polymerization kinetics

💡 This work introduces a low-concentration hydrated eutectic electrolyte (2.45 m KFSI-Bds-H₂O) for aqueous K-ion batteries, achieving a wide 3.7 V stability window, low viscosity, high conductivity, and non-flammability.
